morphology.look_here_first: Start with growth form and the flower/fruit-bearing shoots: creek plum is a low thicket-forming deciduous shrub rather than the small-tree habit typical of Mexican plum. Confirm narrow ovate-lanceolate serrate leaves with glandular teeth/glands, white flowers in small clusters along the branches, and round yellow-to-red plum fruits.
diagnostic_traits: thicket-forming deciduous shrub, commonly about 2–4 m tall
shoots arise clonally from spreading shallow roots
alternate simple leaves, usually narrow ovate-lanceolate
serrate margins with glandular teeth, especially on developing leaves
white flowers in small clusters along the branches
round fleshy drupes ripening yellow to red

key_distinctions: vs. Prunus mexicana: P. rivularis is a smaller, strongly thicket-forming shrub; P. mexicana is usually a small tree with larger plum fruit and more tree-like bark/trunk development.
vs. Prunus serotina: P. rivularis has small branch-borne flower clusters and yellow-to-red plums; P. serotina is a tree with elongated racemes and dark purple-black cherries.
vs. Prunus angustifolia: both can form thickets, so use the existing B074 comparison material and independent review rather than range alone.
